hints.S53_A1: Her memory is compared to a BLADE: she can RECALL THE EXACT SHELF LOCATION of any book WITHIN SECONDS. Ask: is a blade dull and heavy, or keen and precise? Match the adjective to the blade, not to the library.
hints.S53_A2: The stickers are all gone, and the children HAD TO ASK FOR MORE. Ask: which phrasal verb means to use up the entire supply of something? 'Gave up' means to stop trying; 'looked after' means to take care of.
hints.S53_A3: The clue follows the dash: NOT ONE PERSON WAS SPEAKING, NOT EVEN IN A WHISPER. Ask: which adjective means completely without sound? 'Crowded' counts people, and 'colourful' talks about what you see.
hints.S53_A4: The librarian used CLEAR TAPE so that the book COULD STILL BE USED. Ask: which verb means to mend something damaged? 'Tore' would harm it further, and 'replaced' would throw the old page away.
hints.S53_A5: The clue is the list after the dash: OLD HANDWRITTEN LETTERS AND MAPS. Ask: which word covers written records of every kind? 'Paintings', 'medals' and 'photographs' each name one narrow format only.
hints.S53_B1: The subject is SOMEBODY, not the readers sitting around them. Ask: does a word like somebody, anybody or nobody count as one person, or as many? In the present tense, a singular subject needs the -s ending.
hints.S53_B2: HAS is waiting for a partner, and the corner is still there with its BEAN BAGS AND FLOOR CUSHIONS. Ask: after 'has', which form completes a present perfect? This phrasal verb does not change shape in the past participle.
hints.S53_B3: THAN THE OLD ONE shows two buildings being measured against each other. Ask: does a short adjective take -er, or the word 'more'? Putting 'more' in front of a word that already ends in -er is a double comparative.
hints.S53_B4: THE LIBRARIAN ANNOUNCED THE START OF STORY TIME - a short event cutting across a longer one. Ask: which choice shows the students already in the middle of their book reports? A plain past verb reports a finished job.
hints.S53_B5: THAN is sitting in the sentence, so two sections are being compared for quantity. Ask: which word builds a comparison of number with a countable plural? 'Much' and 'a little' both need uncountable nouns.
hints.S53_B6: The statement is already negative: YOU HAVEN'T RETURNED the book. Ask: after a negative statement, is the tag positive or negative? The tag also copies the helping verb that is standing there already.
hints.S53_B7: The book did not act - THIRTY TIMES IN A SINGLE MONTH tells you what people did to it. Ask: which choice makes the subject the receiver of the action, set in the past? The subject is one book, so watch the number.
hints.S53_B8: A reported request: the librarian ASKED THE CHILDREN, and gives a reason - WHILE OTHERS WERE READING. Ask: after 'asked + person', which form follows - the plain verb, the -ing form, or 'to' + verb?
hints.S53_C1: AISHA is one person, and the habit repeats EVERY WEEK WITHOUT FAIL. Ask: in the simple present, does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the verb with -s? Two box forms describe one moment only - not this.
hints.S53_C2: The verb ENJOYS comes first, and the box form must follow it directly. Ask: does 'enjoy' take 'to' + verb, or the -ing form? Same family: finish, avoid, keep and practise all behave in exactly the same way.
hints.S53_C3: LAST SATURDAY is finished time, and the novel was done in a single afternoon. Ask: which box form is the plain past? Careful - this verb is irregular, so its past looks exactly like its base form on paper.
hints.S53_C4: WHILE plus a sudden event - THE LIBRARY LIGHTS FLICKERED - means the longer action had already started. Ask: which box form shows an action still in progress in the past, with a singular subject?
hints.S53_C5: Count the subject: HER TWO YOUNGER BROTHERS - that is more than one. Ask: for an action in progress in the past, which helping verb goes with a plural subject? One brother takes 'was'; two take the other one.
hints.S53_C6: HER LIBRARY TARGET FOR THIS YEAR IS ... - after 'is', an aim is expressed with an infinitive. Ask: which box form begins with the little word 'to'? After it, nothing may be added - no -s, no -ing.
hints.S53_C7: SO FAR means 'up to this moment', so the counting of THIRTY-EIGHT books is still open. Ask: which box form is a present perfect - a helping verb plus a past participle? A plain past would close the period.
hints.S53_C8: RIGHT NOW points at this very moment, not at a habit. Ask: which box form shows an action happening as we speak, with a singular subject? The habit form would mean she does it regularly instead.
hints.S53_D1: Readers move along the shelves FREELY, PICKING UP BOOKS THAT CATCH THEIR EYE, with no fixed plan. The blank follows 'often', so a verb is needed. Ask: which box word means to look casually along the shelves?
hints.S53_D2: The dash defines it: A SEARCHABLE LIST OF EVERY BOOK AVAILABLE, and it is ONLINE. Ask: which box word names that complete list? A 'bookmark' only keeps your place on one page.
hints.S53_D3: The clue is that ENCYCLOPAEDIAS CANNOT BE BORROWED and MUST BE USED INSIDE. Ask: which box word names the section you may only look things up in? 'Fiction' books go home with you.
hints.S53_D4: The dash spells it out: MADE-UP STORIES, borrowed FOR PLEASURE. Ask: which box word names invented writing - novels, fairy tales, adventures? The opposite kind of book is factual and true.
hints.S53_D5: The book was NOT RETURNED BY THE DUE DATE, and A SMALL FINE MAY BE CHARGED. Ask: which box word describes a book that is late? To 'renew' it would have kept it out of trouble.
hints.S53_E1: THE BOOKS is the subject of the underlined verb, and they fill the whole shelf. Ask: does a plural subject take the singular past form of 'to be', or the plural one? Look at the subject, not at the word beside it.
hints.S53_E2: Stretch the underlined word out: 'they are BORROWED BOOKS' makes no sense at all. Ask: which spelling shows that the books belong to the students? The two spellings sound alike, so decide by meaning, not by ear.
hints.S53_E3: The underlined word names the deep sadness felt when HER FAVOURITE LIBRARY WAS CLOSED DOWN, and its vowels are swapped. Ask: with no C in front, which vowel leads? Compare: believe, brief, piece.
hints.S53_E4: SPOKE is the action, and the underlined word answers 'in what manner did she speak?'. Ask: can an adjective ever describe a verb? Manner words are built by adding -ly to the describing word.
hints.S53_E5: Count the owners: the passage speaks of THE LIBRARIAN, one single person, all the way through. Ask: for a single owner, does the apostrophe come before the -s, or after it? The underlined form claims there are many.
hints.S53_F1: 'AS LONG AS' states the condition, so the THIRTY MINUTES A DAY sentence goes first. Ask: does a condition clause ever take 'will'? Keep the future verb for the result half, and put a comma between the two.
hints.S53_F2: The second sentence adds a fact about the same COLLECTION, so it can hang off the first with 'which'. Ask: after 'which', is a pronoun still needed? And which mark separates the extra fact from the main sentence?
